articles.title: APOD: 2026 October 2 – The Complete Sharpless Catalog: 313 Nebulas
articles.description: What does it take to image hundreds of nebulas? Today’s image contains the entire Sharpless Catalog of H II Regions, totaling 313 objects. Zoom in and explore!
articles.summary: A remarkable image captures all 313 nebulas from the Sharpless Catalog, representing an extraordinary feat of astronomical observation. This comprehensive catalog showcases the breathtaking diversity of stellar nurseries.

articles.title: Galaxies in a cosmic house of mirrors
articles.description:
Image:
			
This NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features galaxies in great detail that have been warped and multiplied like they’ve stepped into a house of mirrors. The brilliant golden galaxies splashed across this image belong to a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies concentrated on one side of the cluster are not actually part of the cluster and are much farther away from us.
MACS J0454.1-0300 is itself immensely distant: the light from these galaxies has been travelling to us for so long that we’re seeing the cluster as it was when the Universe was about 8 billion years old. While this galaxy cluster is a valuable scientific target in its own right, the real stars of this image are the galaxies that appear warped and stretched, like a painting that has been smeared by a giant hand.
The way these galaxies look is the result of gravitational lensing, in which the enormous mass of a foreground object such as a galaxy cluster bends and magnifies the light from a more distant object in the background. Gravitational lensing allows astronomers to observe galaxies, star clusters and even individual stars that are too far away for our telescopes to see under normal conditions. While the large, orange galaxies appear obviously distorted, look carefully at some of the small reddish background galaxies throughout this picture: even at the very edges of the frame, there are galaxies whose images have been bent into tiny arcs by MACS J0454.1-0300’s gravity.
The gravitationally lensed areas show multiple images of galaxies from when the Universe was young: a group of galaxies 2 billion years after the Big Bang, and a single galaxy just 800 million years old after the Big Bang. The galaxy group appears to be going through a merger, resulting in an enormous burst of star formation.
Astronomers have also identified individual bright ‘knots’ within the gravitationally lensed areas, corresponding to regions as small as 5 light-years across. These tiny clumps appear magnified by a factor of more than 300, in some cases.
A NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image of this same cluster was released in 2014. Take a moment to compare the two images; the difference between them is dramatic. The new Webb image reveals hundreds of galaxies missing from the earlier image. These galaxies were there all along, but Webb is much more sensitive to their much redder light.
The data behind this image come from two observing programmes (#5058, PI: Furtak; #6882, PI: Fujimoto) that leverage the ability of massive galaxy clusters to bring distant objects into view.
[Image Description: A massive galaxy cluster, made of many golden elliptical galaxies with the largest, brightest one in the centre. Heavily distorted orange galaxies appear all around the cluster, the largest concentrated in a large arc around the cluster's centre; these are images of very distant galaxies, created by gravitational lensing. A few galaxies are large and bluish-white in colour; bright, nearby stars are the same colour.]
Release on esawebb.org
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures galaxies in extraordinary detail through gravitational lensing, revealing intricate cosmic structures. This picture of the month exemplifies how modern astronomy unveils the universe's hidden wonders.

articles.title: NASA's First Selection for a New Class of Mission: The PRIMA Far-Infrared Telescope
articles.description: NASA announced Wednesday a mission to explore the history and evolution of the universe, PRIMA (PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics), is advancing to the next phase of development. This space telescope is the first in a new class of NASA astrophysics missions, called Probe Explorers, within the agency’s longstanding Explorers Program.
articles.summary: NASA has selected PRIMA, a far-infrared telescope mission, to explore the universe's history and evolution. This groundbreaking new class of mission will advance our understanding of cosmic origins and the formation of galaxies.

articles.title: NASA's Hubble Marks its 200,000th Orbit by Watching Lensed Supernova
articles.description: NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope completed its 200,000th orbit around Earth on Sept. 19th and marked this milestone with observations that could help refine astronomers' measurements of cosmic expansion (aka. the Hubble Constant).
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope celebrated its 200,000th orbit around Earth by observing a lensed supernova, demonstrating the observatory's enduring scientific capability. This milestone reflects decades of groundbreaking astronomical discoveries.

articles.title: First Direct Image of Protoplanet Swirling Surrounding Gas
articles.description: The formation and evolution of planets is the driving force behind both where and how we might find life beyond Earth. This complex and lengthy process first begins with a massive ball of gas and dust that swirls until it flattens into a disk, followed by rocks ranging in size from pebbles to kilometer-scale objects clumping together in a process known as accretion, as they too swirl around within the larger disk and form rocky planets closer to the star and the farther out planets collect the gas, ice, and dust that the star couldn’t evaporate. Until now, researchers have been limited to visualizing the swirling gas and dust forming planets through computer models.
articles.summary: Astronomers have captured the first direct image of a protoplanet forming within surrounding gas, revealing planet formation in action. This breakthrough observation illuminates how planets develop and where habitable worlds might exist.

articles.title: NASA’s Roman telescope just opened its planet-hunting eye
articles.description: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope has demonstrated remarkable pointing stability and given its powerful planet-imaging coronagraph its first look at the cosmos. The telescope can already stay locked on a target with precision comparable to aiming a laser at a dime from about 150 miles away. Its coronagraph also captured stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud, confirming that the instrument can produce focused images.
articles.summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope has successfully demonstrated its planet-hunting capabilities with remarkable pointing stability and powerful imaging performance.

articles.title: Powerful simulations reveal how the first stars changed the universe
articles.description: Ultra-detailed simulations are showing how the first stars lit up the dark Universe and seeded space with elements such as carbon, oxygen, and iron. The MEGATRON project could bridge JWST observations of the earliest galaxies with chemical clues preserved in ancient stars today.
articles.summary: Ultra-detailed simulations reveal how the first stars illuminated the dark universe and distributed essential elements throughout space.

articles.title: The Universe Is Full of Tiny Red Dots—and They’re One of Astronomy’s Biggest Discoveries in Decades
articles.description: A new type of object found in the early universe has puzzled astronomers for years, but they may finally have some answers.
articles.summary: Astronomers have made a major breakthrough understanding mysterious tiny red dots in the early universe, one of the most significant astronomical discoveries in decades.

articles.title: La semaine intense de SpaceX : toutes ses fusées utilisées, première orbite du Starship, record américain de vitesse vers l’ISS et mission top secrète
articles.description: SpaceX a lancé ses trois modèles de fusées en moins de quatre jours. Le Starship est parti ce lundi 28 septembre, puis deux Falcon 9 et une Falcon Heavy ont décollé en moins de 13 heures, entre ce jeudi 1er octobre et la nuit suivante. Pour la première fois, …
articles.summary: SpaceX achieves a historic milestone by launching all three rocket models within four days, including Starship's first orbital flight. This unprecedented launch cadence demonstrates SpaceX's expanding operational capabilities and marks multiple records for the company.

articles.title: Quatre tirs en quatre jours : SpaceX fait décoller toutes ses fusées, avec des misions inédites
articles.description: SpaceX a lancé ses trois modèles de fusées en moins de quatre jours. Le Starship est parti ce lundi 28 septembre, puis deux Falcon 9 et une Falcon Heavy ont décollé en moins de 13 heures, entre ce jeudi 1er octobre et la nuit suivante. Pour la première fois, …
articles.summary: SpaceX executes an unprecedented four launches in four days across all three rocket models, including Starship's first orbital mission. This extraordinary operational achievement showcases the company's advancing launch capabilities and mission diversity.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 October 3 – Selfie at Vera Rubin Ridge
articles.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 3 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss   APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Selfie at Vera […]
articles.summary: A stunning selfie captured at Vera Rubin Ridge showcases robotic exploration on Mars. This image combines technical achievement with the wonder of planetary science.

articles.title: Heading Home: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 Concludes Station Science Mission
articles.description: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission is ending, with the crew scheduled to return in early October. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev will head home from the International Space Station after supporting research that benefits life on Earth and prepares humans for missions […]
articles.summary: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 completes its International Space Station mission, advancing human spaceflight capabilities and scientific research in orbit. The crew's work demonstrates the success of public-private partnerships in space exploration.

articles.title: NASA’s DAVINCI Probe Can Stand the Heat
articles.description: The engineering development unit for NASA’s DAVINCI (Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging) probe is photographed prior to a major thermal evaluation. The DAVINCI team put the yoga ball-sized vessel into a ceramic-lined chamber with heat-scorched walls and ratcheted up the temperature to 869 F, or 465 C, over the course […]
articles.summary: NASA's DAVINCI probe undergoes successful pressure and heat testing, preparing for its historic mission to explore Venus's atmosphere. This engineering breakthrough brings us closer to unveiling the mysteries of our neighboring planet.

articles.title: Science begins for Smile
articles.description: On 23 September, the European-Chinese Smile mission was declared ready to start revealing how Earth responds to the wind of charged particles from the Sun. This follows a busy in-space commissioning period since the spacecraft launched on 19 May and reached its target orbit for science operations on 20 June.
articles.summary: The European-Chinese Smile mission officially begins its science operations, studying how Earth's magnetosphere interacts with solar wind. This collaboration marks an exciting new chapter in space weather research.

articles.title: Successful Earth flyby improves Juice’s course to Jupiter
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) skimmed the very outer edge of Earth’s atmosphere on 28 September, using the gravity of our home planet to alter its route to Jupiter using very little fuel.
articles.summary: ESA's Juice spacecraft successfully completes its Earth flyby gravity assist, adjusting its trajectory toward Jupiter. This pivotal maneuver brings us one step closer to exploring the icy moons of the outer solar system.

articles.title: A galaxy spinning out of sync
articles.description:
Image:
			
Though the spiral galaxy in this new image by the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope seems serene, it hides a chaotic secret. This galaxy is NGC 4698, and it lies about 55 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo. It’s one of over one thousand galaxies in the Virgo Cluster, the nearest large cluster of galaxies bound together by gravity.
As a spiral galaxy similar to our own Milky Way galaxy, NGC 4698 has spiral arms that curl around within a thin disc of stars, gas and dust. Its centre is dominated by a galactic bulge.
The diffuse off-white glow of the galaxy’s bulge comes from stars smaller, older, and cooler than the massive blue stars that dot the galaxy’s outer disc. These tightly packed stars orbit a supermassive black hole containing millions of times the Sun’s mass. Scientists have found signs that this black hole is actively growing, drawing gas inward with its gravitational pull.
With a flat, starry disc and diffusely glowing centre, NGC 4698 looks a lot like a typical spiral galaxy — but this galaxy is far from normal. NGC 4698 is one of only a few known spiral galaxies with a bulge that extends out from the disc at a right angle. The elongation is faintly visible in this Hubble image, which shows the ghostly glow of the starry bulge peeking above and below the dusty disc. What’s more, the stars and gas nearest the galaxy’s centre rotate perpendicular to the rest of the disc.
What could cause a galaxy to be so out of sync? Astronomers have found that the culprit likely lies outside the galaxy. If NGC 4698 funneled in gas from an outside source, the newly collected gas could have formed a disc of gas and stars in the galaxy’s centre, at an angle relative to the rest of the disc. Some observations suggest that this galaxy once experienced a minor galactic merger, as evidenced by a short ‘tail’ of hydrogen streaming from one side of the galaxy.
The data used to create this image come from an observing programme (#18103; PI: Thilker) focusing on galaxies in the Virgo Cluster.
[Image Description: A spiral galaxy viewed at an angle, with a bright central bulge and winding spiral arms. The arms form a ring around the galaxy, without appearing to reach its centre. Prominent red-brown dust lanes weave through the arms, which are also dotted with bright blue and reddish regions of star formation. The galaxy is set against a dark background scattered with stars and faint distant galaxies.]
Release on esawebb.org
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope reveals a spiral galaxy with surprising internal dynamics, challenging our understanding of galactic rotation. This discovery unveils the complex physics governing the cosmos.

articles.title: BepiColombo’s Mercury arrival begins - full replay
articles.description:
Video: 
			02:31:10
				
Watch the replay of the livestream originally broadcast on 3 September as ESA/JAXA's BepiColombo mission took the first critical step towards arriving at Mercury.
After travelling through the inner Solar System together for eight years, BepiColombo's Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) will separate from the rest of the stacked spacecraft on 3 September 2026. This marks the beginning of one of the most complex planetary arrival sequences ever attempted by ESA.
Broadcast live from ESA's European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) in Darmstadt, Germany, the programme includes live views from the iconic Main Control Room, expert analysis, behind-the-scenes insights, and the first signal from the spacecraft following separation. 
Livestream schedule (CEST): 

13:45 – Livestream begins 
16:00-16:45 – End of livestream
articles.summary: BepiColombo, the ESA/JAXA spacecraft, has successfully arrived at Mercury and begins its mission to study the planet's surface and magnetic field. This landmark arrival represents a major achievement in exploring our solar system's innermost planet.

articles.title: Asteroid Bennu Has an Identity Crisis, and Jupiter Might Be to Blame
articles.description: Asteroid sample return missions have brought well preserved samples of the early solar system (that hadn’t been roasted in a fireball) back to Earth for the first time. But those samples, like the OSIRIS-REx sample from asteroid (101955) Bennu, sometimes provide more questions than answers. A new paper, published in Science Advances from researchers at ETH Zurich and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, highlights one of those questions - why Bennu appears to have been born in both the inner and outer solar system - and a possible answer to it.
articles.summary: Asteroid Bennu's composition reveals clues about early solar system formation, with sample return missions providing pristine evidence of planetary origins. Jupiter's gravitational influence on Bennu helps scientists understand solar system dynamics and history.

articles.title: Coldest Lava Exoplanet Found to Hold an Atmosphere
articles.description: Exoplanets continue to challenge our understanding of planetary formation, evolution, and whether they might be able to support life as we know it. Scientists often use planets in our solar system as analogs for exoplanets, studying exoplanets with extremely short orbital periods forces scientists to constantly rethink our understanding of what planets can withstand during their lifetimes. One such type of exoplanet that has entered the foray in recent years are “lava world” exoplanets, and especially lava exoplanets that orbit dangerously close to their stars. But while it has been long known that lava worlds on with higher temperatures have atmospheres, “colder” lava worlds have been found to lack atmospheres.
articles.summary: Scientists discovered that the coldest known lava exoplanet retains an atmosphere, challenging conventional models of planetary formation and atmospheric retention. This finding expands possibilities for where life might exist beyond Earth.

articles.title: Q&A: An Earth-like planet with two suns?
articles.description: A nearby star system with two suns could potentially support an Earth-sized planet in a region where liquid water could exist, according to a new paper examining the dynamics of the system.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A nearby binary star system could potentially host an Earth-like planet capable of supporting liquid water, expanding our understanding of habitable worlds. Such systems demonstrate the diversity of planetary environments in our cosmic neighborhood.

articles.title: Milky Way may have begun as thousands of galaxies, new simulations suggest
articles.description: In the early days of the universe, our home looked very different from how it does today. Back then, the region in our universe that would eventually become our Milky Way neighborhood was a collection of thousands of smaller galaxies—some pumping out tons of new stars, others filled only with gas or littered with dead stars and black holes.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: New simulations suggest the Milky Way originated from thousands of smaller galaxies that merged over cosmic time. This revolutionary understanding of galactic evolution reshapes how we view our home galaxy's formation and development.

articles.title: Team selected for NASA program to explore potential lunar cave
articles.description: NASA has selected a Planetary Science Institute–led proposal to investigate whether a potentially large underground cave extends beyond the opening of a lunar pit. Such a cave may one day provide a safe haven for astronauts to escape the radiation and extreme temperature swings present at the lunar surface.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA has selected a team to investigate a potentially large underground lunar cave, advancing exploration of the Moon's geology and potential resources. This mission opens new frontiers in understanding lunar subsurface environments and supporting future human exploration.

articles.title: Black holes may grow quietly alongside galaxies even without violent mergers
articles.description: Astronomers analyzed 2,435 galaxies hosting actively feeding black holes using data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Among them, they identified 546 "bulgeless" galaxies—systems with little or no central stellar bulge. Their paper, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, suggests that galaxies without a central bulge grow black holes just as effectively as galaxies that have one—a surprising sign that black holes don't need galaxy mergers to grow normally.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers discovered that black holes can grow quietly alongside galaxies without violent mergers, expanding our understanding of black hole formation and galaxy evolution. This finding reveals previously unknown pathways for supermassive black hole development.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the lowest-mass double neutron star system to date
articles.description: Neutron stars, the extremely dense remains of massive stars that exploded at the end of their lives, are widely studied astrophysical objects. Some of these stars, known as pulsars, spin and send out beams of radio waves, making them appear to pulse as the beams sweep past Earth.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered the lowest-mass double neutron star system ever observed, advancing our understanding of these extreme cosmic objects.

articles.title: ESA’s Juice just used Earth as a slingshot to Jupiter
articles.description: ESA’s Juice spacecraft raced past Earth on September 28, using our planet’s gravity to dramatically reshape its path toward Jupiter without burning much fuel. The flyby changed its direction by 20 degrees and increased its speed by 3.5 km/s, while also giving scientists a rare chance to test its instruments on Earth and the Moon.
articles.summary: ESA's Juice spacecraft successfully used Earth's gravity as a slingshot on September 28 to redirect its trajectory toward Jupiter.

articles.title: Chang’e-6 lunar soil contains a surprising magnetic time capsule
articles.description: Scientists studying Chang’e-6 lunar soil have discovered a previously unknown magnetic mineral in natural Moon samples: a form of metallic iron called γ-Fe. Found inside tiny impact-glass particles, the nanoscale iron can preserve a stable magnetic signal, potentially acting like a microscopic fossil of the Moon’s long-lost magnetic field.
articles.summary: Analysis of Chang'e-6 lunar soil has revealed a previously unknown magnetic mineral, offering new insights into the Moon's geological history.

articles.title: The early universe wasn’t nearly as pristine as scientists thought
articles.description: JWST has revealed that galaxies were spreading carbon, oxygen, and other heavy elements through space just 500 million years after the Big Bang. The surprising discovery suggests the young universe became chemically enriched much earlier than expected, potentially erasing traces of its very first stars.
articles.summary: JWST observations reveal that the early universe was more chemically enriched than previously thought, with galaxies spreading heavy elements just 500 million years after the Big Bang.

articles.title: A record-breaking X-ray flash may reveal the birth of a magnetar
articles.description: Astronomers have found strong evidence that some mysterious, minutes-long X-ray flashes are produced when two neutron stars collide and create a magnetar. One record-setting event glowed in X-rays for nearly 10 minutes, potentially opening a new way to find these extreme cosmic mergers.
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified strong evidence that mysterious X-ray flashes are produced during magnetar birth events from merging neutron stars.

articles.title: The ice blasting from Saturn's moon Enceladus is stranger than scientists realized
articles.description: Enceladus may naturally separate and concentrate chemicals from its hidden ocean as droplets slowly freeze and shatter on their way into space. The process could explain Cassini’s puzzling ice-grain chemistry while giving future spacecraft a powerful advantage in searching for organic compounds and clues to life.
articles.summary: New research reveals that Saturn's moon Enceladus concentrates chemicals from its subsurface ocean through a natural freezing and crystallization process, with profound implications for ocean world chemistry.

articles.title: China's FAST telescope to advance with Phase II construction as project marks 10th anniversary
articles.description: The Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Radio Telescope (FAST), known as the China's "Sky Eyes", will mark the 10th anniversary of its inauguration on September 25. Since its launch, the facility has achieved a series of landmark scientific and technologica…
articles.summary: China's FAST telescope, the world's largest single-dish radio telescope, advances into Phase II construction as it celebrates its 10th anniversary. The 'Sky Eyes' project continues to expand its capabilities for astronomical discovery and exploration.
